g.text: One PathMap operation on the join engine through the prefix source (P5e, Phase 2)
CLASSIFY: phase A of the transaction
begin over the channels of the routed key
read the config once
check the path of each channel (check_key),
the params and the query of the discipline,
and the arrows and the orders of a join
PathTooDeep, UnsupportedPathElement
or Inconsistent: nothing is staged
yes
a check fails?
no
PREFIX-SCOPE: the own prefixes (a send adds every prefix of its path),
closed under the join groups of each index channel, and every prefix
of every stored datum once a prefix holds a marker (one read of I(ε))
PHASE B: the same transaction locks C(sid), S(sid), D(p) of each data path
and I(q) of each prefix in one sorted call
RUN-JOIN with the prefix source
the key of each channel becomes [0x49] ‖ prefix_key(path)
a join takes its binds in the order of (hash(I(q_i)), i)
TOUCH: an ordered discipline bumps S(sid) once in the transaction,
with S(sid) as both counter channels (shares_counter)
WINDOW(q, need): for each path p ⪰ q in path-key order,
the window of the discipline on D(p), without the datums in flight
OFFER: the waiters of I(p), I(parent(p)), …, I(ε), the most specific first,
one head waiter for each prefix (a refusal moves to the next prefix)
RECEIVE: the greedy search over the windows, the guard once
a waiter fires?
yes
no
one COMM on I(q): the vehicle of the element on the produce side,
the markers of the bound datums on the consume side
the waiter peeks?
yes
no
each bound datum that is not persistent becomes a second send
with restore = depth of q: its marker is owed (Rule E)
retire_spent at every fire site (Single, Offer, Join, Cascade):
RETIRE-PLAN of each spent datum, then RETIRE-CLASS of a set
land: STORE-MARKERS of a fresh element (D(p), then each I(q)),
or the restore of an owed marker with its bytes
park: the waiter on the index channels of its prefixes
FINISH and COMMIT
FINISH: store again each marker that the transaction still owes
(only a stop at FIRE_ROUND_CAP owes one: item O-2, closed)
bump S(sid) once (decision 51)
yes
a bag or a set changed the state?

commit, and re-issue one settle job: the offers of the second sends,
the dirty prefixes and the resume of the operation
commit
Concept colors
the substrate: transactions, lock keys, staging
the prefix source and the join engine: keys, windows, searches
a COMM of a fire, or a quiescent commit
a second send in flight with its owed marker
a retire: K_retire COMMs on single channels
the token, a stored record or marker, or a parked waiter
a failure, or a stop that commits and re-issues
